Contact us today for a FREE Estimate: 801-509-5344 How to Tell If You Need Foundation Repair Foundation Settlement Cracks Horizontal cracks in your foundation may not necessarily mean that you have a serious foundation problem, but it’s worth checking out. Even small cracks can become major issues if left unchecked. Over time, small cracks can lead to larger issues. If you notice large cracks, especially if it’s a horizontal rather than a vertical crack in the basement wall, then we encourage you to get in touch with a member of our team as soon as possible. We’ll be happy to provide a free estimate. Damp Crawl Space A damp crawl space does not automatically mean that you have a foundation problem, since the moisture can be caused by a number of issues. A crawl space vent cover can trap moisture, for instance. However, it might also be caused by moisture that’s entering your home via the foundation, which will indicate that it’s not as structurally sound as it should be. If you have a damp crawl space, give us a call today! Our team is happy to provide FREE consultations and, if need be, FREE estimates. Foundation Wall Cracks Cracks in both the drywall and foundation walls can be signs of structural issues. While drywall cracks may seem minor, they can indicate shifting that impacts your foundation. Cracks in the foundation walls are also concerning and should be inspected by a professional to ensure your home’s stability. Addressing these cracks early can prevent more serious and costly problems down the road. Bowing or Leaning Walls If your walls are bowing or leaning, it’s important to address the issue promptly, as these are common signs of foundation problems. Bowing walls may indicate pressure from the soil surrounding your home or shifting within the foundation itself. You can identify this issue by checking if the walls are misaligned at the top or bottom. If you notice any of these signs, contact us at 801-492-3503 for a professional assessment and appropriate repair solutions. Water in the Basement or Crawl Space Is water pooling in your basement or crawl space? Unaddressed moisture in these areas can create ideal conditions for foundation problems, as temperature fluctuations may cause cracks to form and worsen over time. Eventually, this can lead to more extensive damage, including mold growth, wood rot, and even poor air quality throughout your home. A professional basement waterproofing specialist can not only remove existing water but also implement effective solutions such as interior drainage systems, sump pumps, and vapor barriers to prevent future issues. By taking action now, you can protect your home’s foundation, preserve its value, and create a healthier living environment for you and your family. Misaligned Doors Misaligned doors can be more than just a nuisance—they may signal underlying foundation issues in your home. Difficulty in opening or closing doors, or noticing uneven gaps at the top of doorways, can be signs that your foundation needs attention. If you’re experiencing these problems, it’s important to address them promptly. Contact our team at Rhino Foundation Systems for a thorough assessment and professional support. If you notice larger cracks, cracks spanning multiple bricks, or vertical and zigzagging cracks, it’s essential to take action. These signs could suggest significant structural problems that need professional attention. Primary Causes of Foundation Settlement Foundation settlement occurs when the earth’s soil, upon which the property stands, adjusts to the weight of the construction on top (in this case, the home). While some settlement is normal for new construction, settlement that continues to progress or that occurs unexpectedly should be a source of concern for property owners. There are three primary causes of foundation settlement: Soil Not all soils are the same. If the soil hasn’t been tested and prepared, it can be the cause of foundation problems. Soils can be weak and thus unable to properly support the property’s weight, or they may change due to environmental factors such as increased/decreased moisture content. Water Damage Homes with poor drainage systems or that experience heavy rainfall are more likely to have foundation problems. An excess of moisture under a property can result in the soil becoming unstable. Poor Construction Though rare, foundation issues can occur as a result of poor construction. For instance, if the company that built the house did not test the soil or did not take sufficient measures to properly reinforce the property’s foundations, a brand new home can be at risk for foundation problems. How soil can impact foundations Soil integrity plays a crucial role in the stability of a building’s foundation. Ideally, soil should support the building’s weight while adapting to climate and environmental changes. However, certain soil types struggle to handle heavy loads and shifting conditions, reducing their capacity to provide reliable foundation support. Types of Soil Understanding the type of soil beneath your home is crucial for assessing foundation stability and determining the most effective repair solutions. Each soil type reacts differently to environmental changes and weight loads, which can directly affect your foundation. Clay Soil Clay soil is dense and provides good load-bearing capacity when dry. However, it expands significantly when wet, leading to potential foundation movement, cracks, and structural instability. Proper drainage and piering systems are often needed to mitigate these issues. Sand Soil Sand soil provides good drainage, minimizing the risk of water pooling around your foundation. Unlike clay, it does not expand or contract significantly with moisture changes. However, its loose, granular nature makes it prone to shifting or displacement under heavy loads. Homes built on sandy soil may require stabilization and drainage systems to prevent foundation settling or void formation. Silt Soil Silt soil retains moisture better than sand and provides moderate support when compacted. Unfortunately, it is highly prone to water retention and frost heave, causing foundation settling and shifting. Water management systems and piering are typically necessary to address these challenges. Loam Loam is the ideal soil for foundations due to its balanced composition of clay, sand, and silt. It offers excellent drainage, minimal expansion or contraction, and strong support. While loam is generally stable, proper grading and drainage are still essential to prevent localized water pooling. Understanding your soil type helps determine the best solutions for foundation stability. Rhino Foundation Systems specializes in evaluating soil conditions and delivering tailored repairs to protect your home. Contact us today for an expert assessment! In general, costs tend to range from a few hundred dollars for more minor issues to thousands of dollars for more complicated jobs. It’s worth keeping in mind that while the cost of foundation repair can seem significant, it is nearly always a worthwhile investment since it helps to protect your home’s value and provides long-term structural integrity. Helical Piers & Push Piers Helical piers and push piers are some of the most effective foundation stabilization tools available. Following a consultation, our team will decide which solution is best for your property. Let’s take a look at what they are and what they do. Helical Piers Helical piers are an effective and versatile solution for stabilizing buildings with structural issues. This technique involves heavy-duty steel piers with corkscrew-shaped plates that are driven deep into the ground using hydraulic power, providing exceptional support by transferring the structure’s weight to deeper, more stable soil layers. Suitable for a wide range of soil conditions as well as residential and commercial projects, helical piers can be installed quickly with minimal disruption to the landscape, making them a cost-effective and efficient choice. Their ability to reach varying depths ensures long-term stabilization, while their corrosion-resistant materials provide lasting support. Push Piers Push piers are a reliable and effective solution for addressing foundation issues caused by soil erosion, moisture changes, and settlement. These steel piers are driven deep into the ground to stable, load-bearing layers, transferring the structure’s weight and restoring the foundation to its original position. This process provides immediate stabilization and long-term support, preventing further shifting and structural damage. Push piers are ideal for both residential and commercial projects, offering quick, minimally invasive installation. Get a FREE estimate Why Basement Waterproofing is Essential Your basement is the foundation of your home, making it particularly vulnerable to water infiltration. Common issues caused by moisture include:  Foundation Damage Prolonged exposure to water can weaken your foundation, causing cracks, settling, and structural instability.  Mold and Mildew Growth Excess moisture creates the perfect environment for mold, which can spread throughout your home, compromising air quality and causing health problems such as allergies and respiratory issues. ' Decreased Property Value Persistent water issues can significantly lower your home’s market value, deterring potential buyers.  Increased Energy Costs Damp conditions make it harder to regulate indoor temperatures, leading to higher heating and cooling expenses. Our Comprehensive Approach to Basement Waterproofing At Rhino Foundation Systems, we leave no stone unturned when assessing your property for basement waterproofing. Our detailed evaluation considers: Moisture Sources Identifying whether water is seeping through exterior walls, cracks, or flooring. Signs of Damage Assessing visible issues such as leaks, mold, efflorescence (white powdery residue), or water stains. Severity of Water Intrusion Evaluating how often and how much water is entering your basement. Impact on Surrounding Areas Checking for any water damage to adjacent rooms or structural components. Soil and Grading Conditions Determining if improper grading or soil composition is contributing to the issue.  Get A Free Quotation Contact Us Now Advanced Basement Waterproofing Methods We offer industry-leading waterproofing solutions designed to protect your basement for years to come: Interior Waterproofing Solutions Waterproof Sealants: These high-performance coatings prevent moisture from penetrating walls and floors, creating a protective barrier against leaks and dampness. Interior Drainage Systems: Installed beneath your foundation, these systems collect water and channel it to a sump pump, which efficiently removes it from your home. Interior solutions are ideal for addressing existing water issues without extensive excavation. Exterior Waterproofing Solutions Sealants and Membranes: Applied to the exterior walls of your foundation, these materials form a durable shield against water infiltration. Exterior Drainage Systems: Designed for properties prone to flooding or heavy rainfall, these systems divert water away from your home using French drains, gravel layers, and other drainage mechanisms. This proactive approach is highly effective for homes in high-risk areas. Sump Pump Systems Sump pumps are essential for preventing water from pooling in your basement. Our systems are equipped with advanced technology, such as battery backups, to ensure continuous operation even during power outages. Vapor Barriers Vapor barriers are installed to reduce moisture levels and prevent water vapor from seeping into your basement. These are particularly effective for reducing humidity, which can contribute to mold and mildew growth. Common Signs You Need Basement Waterproofing Not sure if your basement needs waterproofing? Watch for these warning signs: Z Persistent dampness or standing water. Z Musty odors or visible mold growth. Z White, chalky residue (efflorescence) on walls. Z Cracks in foundation walls or floors. Z Water stains or discoloration. If you’ve noticed any of these issues, it’s time to act. The sooner you address water intrusion, the more effectively you can protect your home from long-term damage. With years of experience in the industry, we offer the most effective and durable solutions for concrete sinking or shifting. Get a FREE estimate What is Concrete Lifting? Concrete lifting is the process of restoring sunken or uneven concrete surfaces to their original level and function. Over time, concrete slabs can shift due to changes in soil conditions, moisture levels, and natural settling. This can lead to cracks, uneven surfaces, and dangerous tripping hazards. Concrete leveling addresses these issues by lifting and stabilizing the concrete, improving both its appearance and its structural integrity. At Rhino Foundation Systems, we utilize a cutting-edge polyurethane foam injection method that is fast, efficient, and highly effective in lifting and stabilizing sunken concrete slabs. Our expert team ensures that your property’s concrete surfaces are restored to their original level, eliminating gaps, cracks, and dangerous slopes. How Does Concrete Lifting Work? Concrete Lifting is a precise, multi-step process that involves injecting a specialized polyurethane foam underneath the affected concrete to lift and stabilize it. Here’s how it works: U Assessment and Preparation We begin with a comprehensive inspection to assess the extent of the settling and identify the underlying causes. Our team will mark the areas where the foam injections will be made, ensuring that we target the problem areas for effective lifting.  Drilling Small Injection Holes Small, dime or quarter-sized holes are drilled into the sunken concrete slabs. These holes provide the entry point for our polyurethane foam.  Injection of Polyurethane Foam Our proprietary polyurethane foam is injected beneath the concrete. As the foam expands, it fills the voids beneath the slab, lifting it back to its original position. This foam is lightweight yet highly effective at stabilizing the soil underneath, providing a long-term solution.  Precise Lifting As the foam expands, our technicians carefully monitor the lifting process to ensure the concrete is raised evenly and aligned with the surrounding surfaces. We ensure that all uneven areas are corrected to restore the surface to its proper level.  Completion and Clean-Up Once the concrete is leveled, we remove any remaining injection ports, clean the area, and ensure the surface is smooth and ready for use.  Get A Free Quotation Contact Us Now This method is non-invasive, quick, and minimizes disruption to your property. Why is Concrete Lifting Necessary? Concrete Lifting is necessary because concrete slabs are typically installed on soil, which can shift and settle over time. This movement is often caused by changes in soil moisture, fluctuating temperatures, poor drainage, and natural soil compaction. As a result, concrete slabs can sink, crack, or become uneven. Without intervention, these issues can worsen, leading to more significant damage, increased repair costs, and potential safety hazards. Concrete Lifting addresses these concerns by stabilizing the soil and lifting the concrete back to its original level, restoring both its functionality and appearance. The benefits of Concrete Lifting go beyond cosmetic improvements – it helps extend the lifespan of your concrete surfaces, eliminates tripping hazards, improves drainage, and increases the value of your property by enhancing its curb appeal. Get a FREE estimate The Importance of Managing Excess Water Around Your Home Excess water around your foundation can lead to serious structural damage, mold growth, and even flooding. Whether it’s from heavy rainfall, snowmelt, or poor drainage, the presence of standing water near your home can increase hydrostatic pressure on the foundation, weaken its integrity, and even cause cracks or shifts in the structure. This can lead to costly repairs and reduce the overall value of your home. French drains are an effective way to protect your home from these risks, efficiently redirecting water away from your foundation to maintain its stability and long-term health. The Role of French Drains in Water Management French drains are an innovative solution designed to collect and redirect excess water away from your home’s foundation. They work by intercepting water from the soil and channeling it through a system of pipes, gravel, and stone, providing a reliable way to manage groundwater and surface runoff. At Rhino Foundation Systems, we design and install French drains with precision to ensure optimal functionality, keeping your property safe and dry no matter the weather. How French Drains Work A French drain consists of a perforated pipe, often surrounded by gravel or stone, which is buried underground to create a drainage system. As water collects in the soil around your home, it is naturally drawn to the French drain, where it is then directed away from the property. This process effectively reduces hydrostatic pressure around the foundation, preventing water from entering the basement, crawl space, or foundation walls. The drain channels water safely away from the property, keeping your home dry and reducing the risk of structural damage caused by moisture buildup. Our team ensures that the trench is angled correctly to guide water flow away from the foundation. = Pipe Placement We place a perforated pipe in the trench, which will allow water to flow into the system. The pipe is surrounded by gravel or stone, ensuring that the water is properly filtered before being channeled away from your home. = Backfilling and Final Adjustments After the pipe is placed and secured, we backfill the trench with additional gravel and soil, ensuring that the system is covered and protected. The final system is designed to be effective and unobtrusive, blending seamlessly with the landscape. French drains are installed at an optimal depth to ensure that they can intercept groundwater and surface runoff efficiently. Whether you have clay, sandy, or rocky soil, our experienced team has the knowledge to install the system in the most effective way for your property’s specific conditions. Concrete lifting—also known as slab lifting or slab jacking—is the process of raising and stabilizing concrete surfaces that have sunken due to soil movement, erosion, or compaction. Instead of replacing the slab entirely, we drill small holes and inject specialized materials beneath the concrete. These materials expand to fill voids, gently lifting the slab back to a safe and level position. The result? A smoother, safer surface at a fraction of the time and cost of replacement. Why It Happens in Alpine Alpine’s dramatic temperature swings, snow melt, and seasonal rainfall all contribute to shifting soil conditions. Get a FREE estimate The Importance of Sump Pumps for Flood Prevention A sump pump is a crucial component of any home’s waterproofing system, designed to efficiently collect and expel excess water before it can cause damage. By directing water away from the foundation, a sump pump helps prevent flooding, mold growth, and water damage in basements and crawl spaces. With a properly installed sump pump system, you can protect your home from costly repairs and preserve its structural integrity for years to come. How Sump Pumps Work A sump pump is typically installed in a specially constructed sump pit located in the lowest part of your basement or crawl space. It works by automatically activating when water levels in the pit rise above a set threshold, usually triggered by a float switch. Once activated, the sump pump draws the water from the pit and pumps it out through a discharge pipe, away from the foundation and exterior of your home. The pump continues to operate until the water level recedes to a safe point, at which time it automatically shuts off, ready to resume action if needed. This continuous cycle ensures that your home remains dry and free from the risk of flooding or moisture intrusion, even during heavy rainfall or snowmelt. Sump Pump Installation Process and Expertise At Rhino Foundation Systems, our team of experienced technicians carefully assess your property to determine the best location for your sump pump installation. The pit is carefully sized to accommodate the volume of water expected in your home. Z Sump Pump Selection and Placement We select a sump pump that best meets the requirements of your property, ensuring it has the capacity to handle the potential water load. The pump is then installed in the sump pit, positioned for maximum efficiency.  Pipe Installation After placing the pump, we install a discharge pipe that directs the water away from the home. The pipe is routed to a designated area outside the home to ensure that water is diverted far enough to prevent re-entry into the foundation.  Testing and Final Adjustments Once the sump pump and discharge system are in place, we test the system to ensure it is operating correctly and efficiently. We make any necessary adjustments to optimize the performance of the system.
